levelSelection.withGrammarText: telc Deutsch B1, B2 and C1 Hochschule score grammar directly, in the Sprachbausteine. In telc Deutsch B1 that is 20 items and 10% of the points. The gap-fill exercises here follow the same principle: a gap in the text, several answers, one is correct. In the DSH, the grammar section is called „wissenschaftssprachliche Strukturen“ (academic language structures).
levelSelection.withoutGrammarText: DTZ, Goethe-Zertifikat and TestDaF test reading, listening, writing and speaking. Grammar counts through formal accuracy in writing. For the DTZ this matters even more since 1 November 2026: an overall B1 result now requires at least A2 in writing (§ 10 IntTestV).

faq.q: What are the Sprachbausteine in telc exams?
faq.a: The Sprachbausteine are the scored grammar section of telc Deutsch B1, B2 and C1 Hochschule. You fill gaps in texts by choosing from given answers. In telc Deutsch B1 there are 20 items, worth 10% of the total points.

faq.q: Where does grammar count in DTZ, Goethe-Zertifikat and TestDaF?
faq.a: In writing: DTZ, Goethe-Zertifikat and TestDaF have no separate grammar section, but the formal accuracy of your texts is assessed. Mistakes with endings, word order or tenses therefore cost points.

faq.q: What has changed in the DTZ since 1 November 2026?
faq.a: For an overall B1 result you now also need at least A2 in writing (§ 10 IntTestV). A blank or very weak writing section costs you the B1, even if speaking and listening/reading are at B1.

faq.q: Are the exercises enough to prepare for telc or TestDaF?
faq.a: Not on their own. They train grammar specifically: the Sprachbausteine for telc, and the grammar that counts in writing for TestDaF. Practice reading, listening, speaking and writing itself separately, ideally with official model tests.
Choose a level from A1 to C1 and a topic. You fill the gaps in the text, choose from several answers each time and see straight away whether you are right – with an explanation.
